pick.headline: Kohl presents his ten-point plan for German unity
pick.summary: On November 28, 1989, West German Chancellor Helmut Kohl presented a ten-point program to the Bundestag for overcoming the division of Germany.
pick.significance: The plan was the first open step toward reunification, and surprised allies and Moscow alike.
pick.fbis: East Berlin's ADN reported on November 28 that Egon Krenz, interviewed on West German television, rejected preconditions for negotiations, under FBIS's heading on reaction to Kohl's 10-point program.

alternates.headline: Margaret Thatcher leaves office; John Major succeeds her
alternates.summary: On November 28, 1990, Margaret Thatcher formally resigned as British prime minister and John Major took office.
alternates.significance: Thatcher had been Reagan's closest ally in the late Cold War and one of the first Western leaders to embrace Gorbachev.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union report's contents for early December listed a SOVETSKAYA ROSSIYA article of November 29 assessing John Major as 'Thatcher's man'.
